action_items: OPTIONAL: strip the redundant inner <span> from the week <option> in /app/frontend/src/pages/coach/CoachClientDetail.jsx (~line 492) to silence the hydration warning.
critical_code_review_comments: CartContext.jsx is back to pure localStorage — clean, no Coaches import, no useEffect side-fetches. Good.

MyCoaching.jsx ItemCard: computeVials mirrors backend logic but does NOT handle 'IU' / 'clicks' units (factor null). Card falls back to hiding the vials line, which is acceptable, but the 'Add N to cart' button also disappears (canAdd=false) — customer with such items just sees 'Buy on the shop' link. Consider a subtle helper text when factor is null so customers understand why.
MyCoaching.jsx uses toast(...) without an emoji/status; sonner defaults to plain toast. All good, but for consistency with the rest of the app you may want to switch to toast.success().

coaching_routes._hydrate_protocol hydrates product info per protocol view but doesn't strip visible=false products — if a product is hidden after being prescribed, the customer will still see the card. Minor. Consider marking those items with 'product_unavailable':true and disabling the add button.

test_prescribed_cart.py still tests the legacy /prescribed-cart endpoints — good regression coverage; keep them until backend endpoints are actually removed (they remain callable, just unused by the UI).

rca_of_the_issue: Not a bug fix this iteration — this is a UX pivot. Old design (iterations 5–6): coach clicked 'Push N to cart' → server-side prescribed_carts collection → CartContext useEffect on mount fetched the pushes, called consume, and added locally. Race conditions and StrictMode double-add were mitigated with three overlapping guards. New design (iteration 7, verified): coach protocol is only exposed via GET /coaching/my/protocol with product hydration; MyCoaching.jsx's ItemCard computes vials locally (client-side mirror of backend calculator) and calls CartContext.addItem directly on button click. CartContext no longer touches any coaching endpoints. Zero /prescribed-cart network calls observed on mount, click, or reload. The 'first-any-variant' vial fallback edge case flagged in iteration 5 is now less relevant because the customer explicitly clicks a per-item button (they see the same 'variant_label' the coach set).
